# TASK-013 Activation Log

Append-only activation log owned by TASK-013. It is the durable consumption ledger and the gate-closure register for the TASK-001 task graph. Event rows are never edited or deleted; a correction is recorded as a new entry.

- Owner: `orchestrator` / `gpt`
- Cursor field: `activation.last_consumed_event_seq` in `tasks/blocked/TASK-013-task-record-lifecycle-and-gate-closure.md`
- Dispatch condition: `ingress_seq > activation.last_consumed_event_seq`
- Quiescent condition: `ingress_seq == activation.last_consumed_event_seq`
- Ingress source set, observation rule, and observer ownership: `tasks/TASK-001-DEPENDENCY-GRAPH.md`, section "TASK-013 activation and event-ingress model"

**Provider-reroute decisions ingested at ACT-032.** `HUMAN-005` rerouted TASK-059 DevOps from Claude to GPT after two pre-edit provider-limit refusals; `HUMAN-006` rerouted TASK-013 Orchestrator after one. Their durable decision commits are ledger rows 46 and 45 respectively because batch order is ascending source commit, not decision-number order. Both preserve scope, dependencies, gates, lineages, authority, activation semantics, and dormancy. No closed row was rewritten.

## What this log is, and what it is not

**This log is a ledger of consumption, not a queue.** Each row is written by the activation that consumed the fact it records, in the same commit as that activation's effects and its cursor advance. A row therefore arrives already consumed and already stamped with `consumed_by`; no row is ever edited afterwards, and `consumed_by` is never mutated.

**A ledger row is not an inbox entry.** It is a separate record that **references** an entry by `seq` and `fact_id`. Since `MC-004`, an inbox entry carries no consumption field of any kind and is byte-identical before and after the activation that consumes it; `consumed_by` exists only on the row here. That separation is the correction finding F-401 required.

**Dispatchability is not readable from this file.** It is decided by comparing the cursor with `ingress_seq = max(seq)` over the durable ingress inbox — never a count, never a scan of refs, and never a field read off an entry or a row. The facts themselves are durable Git artifacts that each producing owner creates inside its own write scope. An owner wakes TASK-013 by publishing its own artifact, never by writing here or anywhere else under `tasks/`. **Which dispatch contract is in force is declared in TASK-013's `activation.bootstrap_dispatch_contract` field**, and while it reads `interim-operator-authorized` no claim is made that the durable predicate authorized a dispatch; see `MC-005`.

The event rows below are the entries this log promises never to edit. This explanatory prose and the registers that follow are activation-versioned documentation of the model; every change to the model is recorded as a numbered model-correction entry.

## Ingress epochs

| Epoch | Model | Entries | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scan reachable refs, order by committer timestamp then SHA, `ingress_seq` = the count | `seq` 1 … 6 | **Sealed** by `MC-003` at `ACT-004`. Retained as durable provenance; not reproducible under its own rule, which is why the boundary exists |
| 2 | Durable append-only ingress inbox; `ingress_seq = max(seq)`; identity by `fact_id`; positions assigned once at append | `seq_base = 6`, entries from `seq` 7; currently `seq` 7 … 50 | **Active** |

## Event log

`seq` is a stable monotonic integer. In epoch 1 it was assigned in the observation order that epoch's rule defined. In epoch 2 it is assigned **once, at append time**, in ascending order of `source_commit` identifier within a batch, and is never recomputed from a count, a scan, or a timestamp. `consumed_by` names the activation that consumed the entry and wrote the row; it is written once and never changed.

Epoch-2 rows additionally record `fact_id` and `content_hash`, which are the entry's identity and the hash of its source artifact. Until TASK-026 exists, these rows are the durable record of the inbox.

### The reviewer base for TASK-033, and why no architecture is merged here

TASK-033 must read two things that do not live in the same history: the **task graph and routing context**, which are on `agent/claude/orchestrator/task-013`, and the **architecture target** `468b37b`, which is on `agent/gpt/architect/task-032` and is not an ancestor of this branch. `fe0374c` is not an ancestor of either.

The safe setup, and the one TASK-033's record prescribes:

1. Create `agent/gpt/reviewer/task-033` from the **head of `agent/claude/orchestrator/task-013`** at worktree-creation time, exactly as every earlier reviewer branch in this graph was created. That gives the reviewer the current task records and registers in its working tree.
2. Read the architecture target through **Git object access, not through the working tree** — `git diff fe0374c..468b37b -- docs diagrams`, `git diff 7ff618b..468b37b`, and `git show 468b37b:<path>`. All three branches live in the same clone and share one object store, so every object is readable from any worktree without checkout, merge, or fetch.
3. Resolve the scope-validation base inside that worktree with `git merge-base HEAD agent/claude/orchestrator/task-013` and pass the resolved 40-hex value to `-BaseRef`. Never pass `fe0374c`, `468b37b`, or a review-diff base.

**What must not happen, stated because it is the convenient shortcut.** Merging `agent/gpt/architect/task-032` into the Orchestrator branch, or into the reviewer branch, so that the architecture documents appear in a working tree would put an **unreviewed, unjudged** amendment into a branch whose gate has recorded nothing — and would make it an ancestor of the very record set that is supposed to be gating it. `review` is in TASK-032's `pre_merge_gates`; that gate is open; integration before closure is precisely what the `pre_merge_gates` field exists to prevent. Reading an object is not integrating it. This activation performed step 2 only, and performed no merge of any kind.

### The new requirement, and why it is routed rather than built

The user stated a new requirement in the control session: **routine human GitHub merging must become zero.** After the required independent gates pass, the system should automatically squash-merge the approved task pull request into `integration/autonomous-runtime`, record `branch_integrated`, advance lifecycle state, and dispatch newly ready work — with humans remaining only for explicit policy exceptions such as formal acceptance of a blocking High or Critical security risk, or authorization of an irreversible production action.

**This activation routed it and did not implement, approve, weaken, or presuppose it.**

**Whether the approved architecture already grants the authority was checked rather than assumed, and it does not.** The check was made against `8ea5c32` as integrated at `de3a8d6` and readable on `integration/autonomous-runtime`:

- `COMPONENT-BOUNDARIES.md` names **eight modules with eight owners, and none of them owns merging into the integration branch.** `INTEGRATION-STRATEGY.md` prescribes the merge *method* and *order* — one squash commit per content integration unit, ADR-0010 as amended by ADR-0016, ADR-0041 for the cumulative architecture unit — and its executor is the operator.
- The workspace lifecycle module can publish and **cannot merge, by construction**. ADR-0011 and `WORKSPACE-LIFECYCLE.md` give `executeFinalize` commit, push, and pull-request create-or-update; exactly one function constructs a push, its refspec is `refs/heads/<derivedBranch>`, it takes **no ref parameter**, and a record whose fields would produce another ref is refused before a process is spawned. That is a declared structural prohibition with tests behind it, not a gap to fill in.
- The `branch_integrated` ingress class is typed as produced by "the operator or the runtime's integration step". **The second producer has never existed**; `seq` 4 and `seq` 25 were both operator actions.
- `AGENTS.md` requires each agent to push its task branch and use a pull request, marks governance and enforcement paths human-controlled, and requires human approval for privileged, external, and release-changing actions. Merging into the shared integration branch is external and release-changing.

**So the requirement crosses two prerequisite layers, and both are routed.** The governance layer is registered as the open decision **`HUMAN-004`**, which only a human may record. The architecture layer is routed to a new architect task **TASK-040**, `blocked` on `human_decision(HUMAN-004)` — the second `human_decision` edge this graph has ever carried, and used for the reason the vocabulary states: work an agent is structurally forbidden to unblock. Its review gate is **TASK-041**, under a **new** gate lineage `LIN-INTEGRATION-AUTHORITY-REVIEW` at round 1.

**Why a new lineage rather than `LIN-ARCH-REVIEW` round 9.** `LIN-ARCH-REVIEW`'s cohort is the eight-member remediation chain whose relations all closed together at round 8. A ninth round there would either reopen eight closed relations or silently redefine what a cohort means — a modelling change this role has no authority to make. `LIN-TOOLCHAIN-REVIEW` is the precedent: a separate artifact under the same gate name gets its own lineage. The new lineage's cohort is `{TASK-040}` and it has one round.

**No implementation task exists and none may be created** until TASK-041 records a passing verdict on an amendment authored under a recorded `HUMAN-004`. **No safeguard was weakened**: no structural prohibition, no gate, no verdict, no write scope, and no publication rule changed.

**TASK-018 and TASK-019 do not depend on any of this, and neither is delayed by it.** TASK-018 must never be merged before TASK-019 records a passing verdict — that is TASK-018's own declared `pre_merge_gates: [review]`, it is unchanged, and nothing in the routing above touches it.

### What this activation records, and what it did not do

**It records an approved governance decision and built nothing.** `HUMAN-004` authorizes two merge executors that do not exist, conditionally, after an architecture amendment is approved and an implementation is independently reviewed and security-validated. **No executor was implemented, no implementation task was created, no merge was performed or simulated, pull request 20 is open and untouched, and no gate, verdict, write scope, structural prohibition, or governance file changed.**

**This is the fourth variant of the overclaim this log keeps naming, and it is the one this activation was most exposed to.** `ACT-006` recorded that an approval is not an implementation; `ACT-007` that a publication is not an approval; `ACT-008` that a satisfied subset of checks is not a verdict; `ACT-017` that an integrated contract is not an implemented capability. `HUMAN-004` is an **approval of a capability**, and its own text is explicit that the authority "becomes operational only after" four separate conditions. A reader who takes the decision as the capability would conclude that merging is now automatic. It is not, and nothing in this activation's effects says it is.

### The decision, transcribed in scope rather than paraphrased into a design

`HUMAN-004` is durable as commit **`7dc07488a5b1cac8b1327ebd63bf747adbe03c68`** `docs: approve autonomous merge authority` on the non-agent branch `human/decision/human-004-autonomous-merge`, published at `origin`, adding exactly one path, `plans/decisions/HUMAN-004-autonomous-merge-authority.md`. Status `approved`, decision date 2026-08-06, decision owner the repository owner, applying to "routine pull-request integration and release-branch promotion".

| Boundary the decision sets | What it says |
|---|---|
| **The authority granted** | Two components. **(1)** A **runtime-owned post-gate integration executor** may squash-merge an approved task pull request into the configured integration branch, currently `integration/autonomous-runtime`. **(2)** A **DevOps-owned release merge executor** may merge the approved integration pull request into `main` after every declared aggregate gate and release-readiness check passes |
| **The condition on it** | "This authority is conditional. It becomes operational only after the architecture amendment is independently approved, the implementation is independently reviewed and security-validated, the required GitHub controls are configured, and the automated checks demonstrate that the executors cannot bypass their admission predicates" |
| **The required normal flow for a task branch** | Read the authoritative task record and immutable publication facts; confirm every declared pre-merge gate is closed with an authoritative passing verdict; confirm no unresolved blocking High or Critical security finding applies; confirm target branch, base branch, head commit, integration order, and merge method exactly match the approved contracts; **persist merge intent before the external side effect**; squash-merge through the GitHub API **without bypassing branch protection**; verify the resulting tree and record the durable `branch_integrated` ingress fact; let the ordinary scheduler advance lifecycle state and dispatch newly ready work |
| **The required normal flow for the release merge** | The same fail-closed pattern, and additionally confirm that all aggregate review, security, QA, performance, documentation, deployment, and rollback requirements declared for the release are complete |
| **Conflict and failure handling** | A merge conflict, stale head, missing check, ambiguous state, API failure, or unverifiable result "must not create a routine human merge request". The executor fails closed, preserves evidence, and routes a remediation task to the responsible agent role. It may retry only under the approved bounded retry policy, and "must never guess, force a merge, or silently discard a conflicting change" |
| **The residual human exception set — finite, and routine merges are explicitly not in it** | Exactly three: formal acceptance of an unresolved blocking High or Critical security risk; authorization of an irreversible production action when deployment policy explicitly requires it, with the explicit note that "a merge to `main` is not itself such an action unless a later approved policy deliberately couples it to an irreversible production change"; and granting, rotating, or revoking credentials and changing repository governance, branch-protection, or authorization policy. When a case "cannot be classified conclusively as outside this set, automation must refuse it and emit a typed exception record. It must not broaden its own authority" |
| **Prohibited capabilities — eight, and neither executor may do any of them** | Author, approve, close, override, or formally accept a gate on work it merges; merge a pull request whose declared pre-merge gates are open or failing; push directly to `main` or set `ALLOW_MAIN_PUSH`; force-push, bypass hooks or branch protection, use an administrator override, or disable a required check; merge governance or enforcement changes under its own authority; release another execution's lock or modify task ownership to make a merge admissible; use a mutable branch head where the contract requires an immutable commit; treat a missing, skipped, timed-out, or cancelled check as passing |
| **Credentials and GitHub controls** | A least-privilege repository credential, preferably a GitHub App installation token with short lifetime and auditable identity, kept outside the repository. "Branch protection and required checks remain authoritative; automation receives merge permission but no bypass permission." Idempotency keys and durable intent/result records must prevent duplicate side effects after retries or restarts |
| **Governance and architecture changes authorized, subject to their normal independent gates** | Amend `AGENTS.md` so the mandatory protocol permits the two named executors' narrowly scoped post-gate merges while preserving the prohibition on direct pushes and gate self-approval; amend the runtime architecture, ADRs, diagrams, and integration strategy to define admission predicates, refusal results, durable evidence, recovery, and ownership for **both** executors; add implementation tasks owned **separately** by `runtime` and `devops` after the architecture amendment passes independent review; add independent reviewer, security, QA, and failure-injection validation tasks; configure GitHub branch protection, required checks, merge permissions, and least-privilege credentials |
| **Role assignment** | "No role reassignment is required by this decision. `config/agents/settings.yaml` changes only if an approved architecture later demonstrates that a declared write scope must change; such a change remains human-controlled" |
| **Sequencing** | Five steps: TASK-013 records the commit as a `human_decision_recorded` ingress fact and moves TASK-040 to `ready`; TASK-040 authors the amendment and **must cover task-to-integration and integration-to-`main` automation**; TASK-041 independently reviews it; **only a passing TASK-041 verdict permits the Orchestrator to create implementation and validation tasks**; existing pull requests continue to obey their current gates, and "this decision does not retroactively authorize a gate bypass" |

**What the decision does not do, read from its own text rather than inferred.** It does not merge anything. It does not close, weaken, or reorder a gate. It does not authorize merging pull request 20 before TASK-019 passes — its sequencing clause says the opposite in terms. It does not change `config/agents/settings.yaml`, and it does not itself amend `AGENTS.md`; it authorizes an amendment that remains subject to normal gates and that no `agent/*` branch may author, because `AGENTS.md` is a human-controlled enforcement path.

### What the decision changed on TASK-040, and what it did not

TASK-040 was authored at `ACT-018` against the requirement as the user had then stated it — **task branch into the integration branch**. `HUMAN-004` authorizes **two** executors, and the second one, `integration/autonomous-runtime` into `main`, is owned by a different role and crosses a different safeguard. This activation therefore expanded TASK-040's scope and acceptance criteria to cover both, and expanded TASK-041's review scope to match, because a reviewer whose scope names only one executor would pass an amendment covering half the decision.

**Role ownership boundaries are preserved rather than merged.** The decision assigns the first executor to `runtime` and the second to `devops` and requires their implementation tasks to be owned **separately**; TASK-040 authors the contract for both, which is architecture work and is the architect's, and it names one owning module and one owner **role** per executor. Where the DevOps executor's source path would fall outside `assignments.devops.write_scope` as it stands, that is a **write-scope question returned to the Orchestrator and then to the user**, not something the amendment may decide for itself — the same rule TASK-026's placement already carries, and the decision's own settings clause says such a change remains human-controlled.

**Two obligations were added that neither the decision nor the earlier record stated, and both are refusals rather than expansions.** First, the `AGENTS.md` amendment the decision authorizes is **out of scope for TASK-040**: the architect's write scope does not contain it, and governance and enforcement files cannot be changed from an `agent/*` branch. TASK-040 must state what the amendment has to say and return it; it must not author it. Second, the amendment must state the **release** executor's relationship to the existing `pre_merge_gates` model, because this graph has never declared an aggregate release gate and the decision names one.

### One observation recorded and deliberately NOT made a finding

**The control session closed eight pull requests unmerged, and this activation records the current state where a live record requires it without treating the closure as an ingress fact.** Pull requests 15, 23, 26, 27, 29, 30, 31, and 32 are `CLOSED` with `mergedAt` `null`. **A pull-request state change is not a member of the closed epoch-2 ingress source set.** It is not a commit on a non-agent branch, not a merge on `integration/autonomous-runtime` or of that branch into `main`, not a commit adding a gate report, not a remediation publication, not a dependency-unsatisfiable handoff, and not an owner's named published commit — so **no entry was appended, no class was invented, and `ingress_seq` is unaffected.** This is the same treatment `ACT-029` gave TASK-055's non-execution, and it is the property that makes a content-addressed ingress model able to express "nothing happened" rather than leave a silent gap.

**What it changes about the durable facts: nothing, and that is checkable rather than asserted.** Every source branch survives on `origin` and locally, every published commit those pull requests carried is still reachable, and every `published_commit` this graph records still resolves. **`publication_class` `runtime` requires "an open or updated pull request"**, and pull request 30 — TASK-049's — is now closed, so **TASK-049's recorded publication state is affected and is corrected on its own record to say so.** That correction changes **no** verdict, **no** relation, **no** gate, and **no** integrability: TASK-049 was already non-integrable with both pre-merge gates open at `changes-required`, and it is non-integrable now for exactly the same reason. **The `review_ready(TASK-049)` edge was satisfied at `ACT-028` and consumed then; a satisfied edge is not re-evaluated retroactively**, and TASK-055's target binding to `9fb2eb0c` is immutable and unaffected.

**Whether a `runtime`-class publication whose pull request is later closed should be re-recorded as something other than `published`, and whether the publication-classes rule needs a fourth clause for a withdrawn pull request, are questions about the model that this role is not going to settle inside the activation that first met them.** They are **routed to the next `LIN-DECOMP-REVIEW` round** as an explicit question, in the same way `MC-011`, `MC-015`, `MC-018`, and `MC-019` each routed the question behind the rule they added. **It is deliberately not numbered `MC-`**, because no rule changed and no earlier claim was false when written. **It is deliberately not a finding**, because authoring one is not this role's authority.

### One observation recorded and deliberately NOT made a finding

**Two source files at the target contain literal NUL bytes, and one of them is therefore classified as binary by Git.** `scripts/release/integration-merge/gate-admissibility.ts` contains **8** NUL bytes at offsets 2610 … 2797 and 3733, 3803, and `published-head-evidence.ts` contains **1** at offset 13093. In every case the byte is a deliberate separator inside a template-literal composite sort key — `` `${left.lineage}\0${left.gate}\0${String(left.lineageRound).padStart(9,'0')}\0${left.verdictCommit}` `` and `` `${left.findingId}\0${left.evidenceDigest}` `` — which is the standard idiom for an unambiguous joined key and is plausibly a direct consequence of the permutation-independence the round-1 findings required.

**Three checkable consequences are recorded, and none is characterized as a defect.** First, because `gate-admissibility.ts`'s first NUL falls within Git's 8000-byte binary-detection window, `git diff --numstat` reports `-` / `-` for it and **`--text` does not change that**, so Git's own summary of `26 files changed, 5638 insertions(+), 641 deletions(-)` covers 26 paths but counts lines over only 25 of them; a text-forced recomputation gives that file **+146 / -4**, which would make the full-line view **5784 / 645**. **Both views are recorded because they disagree**, exactly as the rename views were recorded at `ACT-025` and `ACT-029`; the tree is what the commit records and the line counts are a display property. `published-head-evidence.ts`'s single NUL falls past the window, so it is still diffed as text at `239 / 0`. Second, **this property is NEW at TASK-056**: at `9fb2eb0c` no file in the module contained a NUL byte and `git diff --numstat d63864bc 9fb2eb0c` classified none as binary, so round 1 never saw it. Third, a binary-classified file is not rendered as a line diff by Git or by the pull-request UI, which bears on how the delta can be read.

**This role states the fact and stops there.** Whether embedded NUL bytes in a TypeScript source file are acceptable under the approved contract, whether a key-joining separator should be a printable sentinel instead, and whether binary classification of a file in a security-critical admission path impairs reviewability are **review and security judgments**, and the Orchestrator has no authority to make a finding. It is written onto **TASK-057 and TASK-058** so those rounds **decide** it, in the same way `ACT-025` recorded the tautological seventh control command for TASK-047 and `ACT-028` recorded what the 405 and the 11 meant together for TASK-053 and TASK-055.

**It records two independent verdicts against one artifact, and both required changes.** TASK-053 recorded `LIN-RELEASE-EXECUTOR-REVIEW` round 1 at `7e78f1405e40e29034673944949c3851e466cf3c` and TASK-054 recorded `LIN-RELEASE-EXECUTOR-SECURITY` round 1 at `8b2da2f88d38872ded14bc18b739c6586ec47336`. **Both are `changes-required`, both relations stay OPEN, and TASK-049 is not integrable.** **TASK-053 and TASK-054 move `ready` → `done`; TASK-049 stays in `review` at its own immutable head; TASK-055 stays `ready` with no verdict; and three records were created — TASK-056, TASK-057, and TASK-058.**

**Two verdicts, sixteen findings, one owner, one remediation record — and that is a rule rather than a convenience.** Every one of the sixteen names `devops`, read one line at a time from the two reports rather than from either report's summary sentence. The graph requires one remediation task **per responsible owner**, reusing that owner's original non-overlapping write scope. Two records would declare the **identical** scope `scripts/release/integration-merge/**`, which `allow_overlapping_write_scopes: false` forbids, would contend on one lock, could not run in parallel, and would divide one module's admission path between two authors — which the findings-return path names as "as much a defect as folding two owners into one". **The symmetry is exercised in both directions now**: `ACT-021` created **two** remediation tasks for TASK-041's four findings because they named **two** owner roles, `ACT-023` created **one** for TASK-044's three because they named one, and `ACT-029` creates **one** for sixteen across **two reports** because they name one.

**Why two implementation tasks and not one.** `HUMAN-004` authorizes two merges with two owners; the approved architecture states the two authorities "are intentionally not a single executor parameterized by a target ref" and assigns them different source trees, credentials, admission predicates, and protected bases; and round 3 states the requirement explicitly. **Collapsing them would be the mirror of the error `ACT-021` avoided** when one report named two owner roles and produced two tasks.

**Why three gate tasks per executor and not one.** `HUMAN-004` names independent review **and** security validation as separate conditions, the approved `MergeExecutorActivationRecord` carries `implementationReview` and `implementationSecurityReview` as **two distinct immutable members**, and the approved fixture list says the twelve items must be validated by "independent review/security/QA". One task cannot produce three independent verdicts, and this graph gives each gate name its own lineage, round, and owner role. **Six gate tasks, six owner roles across three LLM families, six new lineages.**

**Why review and security block integration while QA does not.** `review` and `security` are in each executor's `pre_merge_gates`; `qa` is not. The approved architecture names a `dormant-before-durable-merge-ingress` contract under which executor source may land dormant, and fixture item 7 requires **live** protected-branch tests that cannot run until the human-controlled control plane is provisioned. Making QA pre-merge would make landing dormant code depend on a provisioning step no agent may perform. **Integration is not activation**: `negativeCapabilityTestAttestation` is an activation member, so until the QA gate passes each executor returns `AuthorityNotActivated` whatever has been merged. Both QA pairs are registered in the aggregate and retrospective gate register with their reason and their recorded risk.

**Self-review is prohibited and the prohibition is checked per pair rather than asserted.** TASK-048 is `runtime` / `claude` and TASK-049 is `devops` / `claude`; their six gate owners are `gpt` and `gemini`. **Every author-and-gate pair here differs in role, in execution context, and in LLM family** — the repository's *preferred* separation, which `LIN-ARCH-REVIEW` and `LIN-INTEGRATION-AUTHORITY-REVIEW` have not had since `HUMAN-003`. Each gate record additionally forbids running in the sibling executor's gate contexts, because the two executors implement one shared normative protocol.

This role transcribed both, closed the one relation that closed, kept the two that did not, routed the three new findings, and created the successor round. **No verdict was produced, softened, split, merged, or anticipated, no finding was resolved or re-dispositioned by this role, no implementation or validation task for either merge executor was created, no architecture, script, or source file was edited, and no pull request was merged.**

**This is the first activation in this graph to close a gate on a first round, and the first to close one and leave two open in the same commit.** `LIN-CI-EVIDENCE-REVIEW` round 1 recorded `approved`, so `(TASK-043, review, round 1)` is **CLOSED** and TASK-043 is **integrable**: pull request 24 may be merged, by the operator, and this activation did not merge it. `LIN-INTEGRATION-AUTHORITY-REVIEW` round 2 recorded `changes-required`, so `(TASK-042, review, round 1)` and `(TASK-040, review, round 2)` **stay open together** and both TASK-040 and TASK-042 remain **not integrable**. **A closed gate on one lineage says nothing about another**, and the two outcomes are recorded side by side without either being read as evidence for the other — which is exactly the property `ACT-021` and `ACT-022` cited when they declined to merge the two lineages into one gate task.

**Integrable is not integrated, and `done` is not either.** TASK-043's every declared gate is now closed, and it stays in `review` because it has not been merged. The graph's own rule is that a record moves to `done` when every gate in its `gate_tasks` is closed **and** the task is integrated; integration is a separate externally visible operation performed by the operator, producing its own `branch_integrated` ingress fact for a later activation. **This activation performed no merge and simulated none.** The distinction is the same one `ACT-016` recorded for the eight architecture records, which stayed in `review` for one activation after their gate closed and moved to `done` only when `ACT-017` consumed the operator's integration.
